reason: Under the schedule and feasibility lens the idea survives. It can be built as a text patch in about 1-2 h of agent work with no GPU, no new weights and no new Kaggle dataset, and it can be scored as a rider before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC with P ~0.75. Checks: (1) CODE. In exp56/x138 cell 4 the 'lowdet peaks' and 'lowdet write' edits are string literals in one patch list that runs BEFORE the V1284 patch. The V1284 patch adds `from v1284_coordinate_refinement import refine as _v1284_refine` at the top of the predict script, so `_v1284_refine`, `ds_path`, `t`, `unet_out[:, f_idx]` are in scope where `_low` is built. The refine module works in the downsampled detector grid (SPACING 1.625 um isotropic), the same grid as `_low` before the `*= downsample` scaling, so the call is valid on the pool. I simulated it in memory on experiments/exp56_x138_verbatim/exp56-x138-verbatim.ipynb cell 4. Anchor `_LOWDET.append((_low.astype(np.float32), _lsc.astype(np.float32)))` count = 1 and anchor `_lc = _lc.astype(np.int16)\n` count = 1. The patched cell compiles, and the coord_offset anchor that V1284 needs is still emitted once in the predict script. Cell 5 load_low_detections reads low_coords as float64, readmit writes float(vox), and no other cell reads low_coords, so floats flow through. (2) NUMBERS. 1,337 readmitted of 121,777 raw nodes, and 479 of 513 pruned leaves were readmitted (CONTEXT.md L1515-1516). Head mean shift 0.739 um, max 1.610 um (DIFF.md s4). Knobs are READMIT_MIN_SCORE 0.965, READMIT_RADIUS 4, GAPFILL_MIN_SCORE 0.5, EXCLUDE 2.0, MAX_ADDED_FRAC 0.03, LOWDET 0.3 (x138 cell 0). All match. (3) MECHANISM, one correction. READMIT_MIN_SCORE equals the detector threshold (0.965), and the pooled local-max peak set does not depend on the threshold. So readmitted nodes are UNREFINED copies of above-threshold peaks that the head already refined before the ILP. Refining the pool reproduces exactly those coordinates for readmit, in distribution. Only the 0.5-0.965 gapfill peaks are sub-threshold, and for them the head is out of distribution and its effect has not been measured. (4) SCHEDULE WEAKNESSES. (a) Validation step (2), the lab replay with friend A's x138 cache, cannot be scheduled: no x138 lab cache exists, friend A has been silent since 24 Sep, and readmit/gapfill replay needs pools dumped at run time. Only the structural dummy checks remain. (b) It is not tied to the runtime-guard probe itself: that sibling verdict (v_kaggle-intel_runtime-guard-audit_schedule.json) ships the guard as a --set rider on every x138-family candidate. The real host is therefore whatever x138-family F1 candidate is submitted 26-28 Sep. (c) tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 allows only divinsert and leafprune, so a new 'lowrefine' patch entry is needed (it is not an env knob in x138 today). (d) The LB cannot attribute it. At +0.0003 against noise 0.003 a scored probe validates only 'no crash, no gross harm'. (e) CSV output rounds coords to int (CONTEXT.md L1431), so the float precision matters only through relink and gapfill decisions, not through written positions (unless floatout is also on). Dependency chain probability: P(#34 confirms x138 as base) ~0.85-0.9 x P(patch clean on dummy) ~0.95 x P(an x138-family host is rebuilt, dummy-run and approved by 29 Sep ~01:00 UTC) ~0.9 = ~0.73-0.77. That is at or above the 0.70 bar, but thin. If #34 fails, there is no x138 host and the idea is moot.
fix_if_any: (i) Implement as `--patch lowrefine` in tools/build_probe_kernel.py, added to BASES['x138']['patches'] (the 'off' state is then byte-identical by construction; with no patch the build equals exp56/exp57b). It makes two exact-once replacements inside the cell-4 'lowdet' literals: replace `_LOWDET.append((_low.astype(np.float32), _lsc.astype(np.float32)))` with a version that refines AFTER the score lookup. The safe variant refines only `_lsc >= 0.965` (in distribution; it exactly reproduces the pre-ILP refined coordinates of the readmit candidates). The full variant is `_v1284_refine(ds_path, t, _low, unet_out[:, f_idx])`. Also delete `_lc = _lc.astype(np.int16)`. Keep the patch ORDER unchanged (lowdet first, V1284 second). Re-ordering reproduces x122's silent 'LOW-DETECTION DUMP SKIPPED' bug. (ii) Tests in the container: anchor counts == 1, the patched cell compiles, the patched predict-script fragment compiles, and the V1284 anchor counts are unchanged. A CPU unit test on a synthetic integer pool checks float32 output, frame column unchanged and shift < 2 um. (iii) FAIL-LOUD dummy gate (the dump patch sits in a non-fatal try/except): require 'Low-detection dump applied'. Require per-video 'LOWDET <name>: N peaks' equal to exp56's N, and raw nodes == 121,777. Readmitted must be 1,337 +-10% and gapfill counts +-10%. Any 'LOW-DETECTION DUMP SKIPPED', 'gap filler idle', 'readmit skipped', 'invalid V1284 displacement' or 'REPAIR FAILED' is a hard fail. Diff against out_exp56 with scratchpad/cmp57.py: only readmit/gapfill nodes and their incident edges may differ. (iv) Host: any x138-family candidate built on 26-28 Sep, together with --set REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=36000. Never give it its own slot. Drop the lab-replay step.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0002 (0 to +0.0008); invisible at LB noise 0.003. The readmit part is only ~1.1% of nodes and the shift is <= 1.6 um inside a 4 um readmit radius and 7 um match radius.
realistic_private_gain: +0.0002 (-0.0003 to +0.0008). The >=0.965-only variant is essentially risk-free because it reproduces coordinates the head already produced. The full variant carries a small out-of-distribution sign risk on the 0.5-0.965 gapfill peaks.
